verdict.justification: B is preferable because its transition-cost analysis correctly includes Juvoxa’s unrecovered upfront payment, a material cost of replacing an already-paid supplier. Both deliverables correctly calculate the quoted programme costs and Vendrax’s INR 510.17 million advantage over Autonexis, but A reports an increase of only “INR 290.79 Mn” after the refund, omitting the original INR 12 million sunk payment from the replacement scenario. B instead adds the INR 8.40 million unrecovered payment to the new-supplier cost difference, producing the correct INR 302.79 million incremental impact under the stated payment assumption. B also provides a stronger executive summary, a clearer transition-cost breakdown, and explicitly identifies assumptions about payments, quotation validity, and unquantified launch losses. Its supplier email covers the required termination, breach, commercial impact, and refund request without A’s unfinished instruction to insert contract references before sending. B does overstate timeline certainty with “6 weeks; no added delay,” whereas A more appropriately distinguishes quoted lead time from unconfirmed tooling and validation schedules, but that weakness does not outweigh B’s materially better financial analysis.
